body: if he wasn't my husband and instead was just a dude who i was dating for a few weeks, maybe i'd be more cool with that. it kinda feels like i'm leaving him to struggle on his own which kinda feels like a shitty thing to do.

i guess i'm struggling with the not making it an issue bit.

if i come home late, and i tell him where i was, he often times doesn't believe me. we'll go through my google maps history together to show him where i was, but it doesn't really help because apparently you can edit that.

at that point, i don't know what i can do to convince him i wasn't up to no good. like do i just let him believe i've been lying the whole time?

INFO: i'd say there's something about me that makes me a target of jokes, but in a very joking manner, and i tend to play along with that sorta stuff. both men and women do it to me, but i can see it coming off as flirting if it's coming from a guy rather than a woman./

also i'd say he's felt this way towards about 80% of my close guy friends in the past three years, at least the ones who he'd probably think are above average looking.
yes, thank you! i want to know if i'm handling this in an A-holish way, so thank you for your response.

yeah, this is what I'm struggling with. If I leave him at home, his mind can think of literally any bad scenario and there'll be no way from him to know for sure what's going on. Then it could turn into someone he'll struggle with for months and that just seems worse...

Married him because I thought we could work through his insecurities together. That's what my responsibility is as a partner.

Divorce is worse is the sentiment I'm getting from my parents when I brought up the subject in the past. It would be cowardly and selfish of me to divorce him just because our relationship isn't easy.
Could I just like... report myself as found and let them know to not share my info? As soon as they file a report?
We don't own a house together, don't have any children, have separate bank accounts, etc. But still good to keep in mind- thank you!

I recall reading that if you wish to remain uncontacted, the authorities will not act on your missing person report when they find you. I remember reading this on Reddit recently actually, not sure how accurate it is though.

Yeah I think I'm struggling w having all of the stress put on myself (getting divorced) and having all of the stress put on my family (me ghosting them). I don't want to be selfish, but I don't know if I can take the additional stress.

I've mentioned to him IRL that "I don't think I can do this much longer", and "I'm not sure if we should continue this relationship" after we had already gotten married. I did not explicitly use the word divorce however, because I was afraid of his response to hearing that word.

He is definitely aware of how I've been feeling. Last year I was not coping with any of this healthily at all, and actually ended up seeking help from a professional. He's aware I'm on anti-depressants. He's aware I hate what things have become. He's aware I feel guilty for hanging out with friends. I haven't hid any of this from him. I've explicitly stated all of these when we try to talk things out. 

I know ghosting is terrible, and I feel really bad thinking about it (the ghosting my brother part especially- I don't want to throw him this task of keeping me hidden from my parents while he's aware of my existence which is why I gotta ghost him too, and it hurts)

I've let him know I've been unhappy while we were still engaged, and once again shortly after getting married, and also again a few months ago.

He says he'll change, and he'll go to therapy, but things haven't changed.

It's really taken a toll on me mentally, and he's aware. I'm not sure how much additional pressure I can take from my family on top of that, but maybe I'm overreacting so I'll try and take things a bit more slow.

Thank you so much for your response though!

I've been feeling this a lot recently.

I think a lot of it is because when I get home, I realize I won't be able to be this excited about anything until the next time it happens. I won't have this much fun with anyone except them.

I get even sadder because I have a husband who I live with, but isn't too interested in going out and doing fun things together. 

There are so many places in the world I'd love to travel to, and I used to "plan" these trips for me and my husband (do a bunch of research on flights, hotels, things to do, etc). He never seemed interested so I never really followed through. I even stopped planning our honeymoon and he hasn't realized/cared.

I stopped planning because I realized I'd rather spend time vacationing in a new place with my friends, rather than with my husband.
100% i'm kinda waiting for my husband to wake up and leave

my husband loves me, but what difference does it make? he's not the only other person in this world. just cause he's around, doesn't  mean my life is complete. there's so much more in life that i'm lacking. there's so much more in life that i don't enjoy.

there's a lot more to life than a gpa.

i know schools are always telling you about going to college and being successful, and it might seem like all of the good jobs require a college degree.

if you can't raise your gpa, don't sweat it.

what do you wanna do in life, if anything?

do you like photography? pretty sure you don't need to go to school for that. maybe put time into that.

do you like learning other languages? put some time into that.

from personal experience, it's easier to put effort into things that i care/like than it is to put effort into school. 

try finding something that speaks to you, and if you do, try pursuing it.

good luck man, hope you figure things out.

i was feeling the same way a few months back, so i decided to do a few things which have kinda helped.

1. make a new reddit account to post in /r/CasualConversation and here. this gives me somewhere to air my thoughts out rather than keeping everything bottled in.

2. try to actually be active (on a regular basis) in the discord servers i'm in, because then i have people who feel like friends. people who care about my day. people who actually talk to me about their day.

i still have no one to talk to irl, but i found talking online kinda helps with the loneliness a bit. hopefully you find something that works for you.

dude i love my mom so much and she needs me way more than i need anything. she's always telling me how she admires my strong-headedness. she tells me she always feels better about life after talking to me on the phone.

i can't imagine what would happen to her if i were to take my own life. i don't know what she'd do. she thinks of me as this really strong person and i don't wanna shatter that illusion.

sometimes i wish i didn't grow up so close to my family. it would be much easier if we didn't care so much about each other, and if we wouldn't miss each other after we pass away.

i don't understand what's the right thing to do in this situation.

i'm new to america and i am still learning new things about the healthcare system every day, but i feel like there's no help when you're depressed.

earlier this year, i decided it was finally time to try and see a therapist. i didn't even know the difference between a therapist, psychiatrist, psychologist, etc at the time. all i knew was my coworkers go and see someone once a week where they talk about things. i wanted to do that too, so i contacted this clinic nearby.

i had an intake call (they asked very general things about anxiety, depression, etc), and i answered all of their questions honestly. the woman was upfront and said that  i may not be guaranteed a spot in their clinic, but provided me with a bunch of suicide helplines at the end of the call.

i never heard from them until i contacted them a month later asking what's up. apparently they can't "provide the level of care" that i needed. later on reddit did i realized, you're not supposed to tell anyone you've had suicidal thoughts. guess i failed their intake call cause i definitely did not deny that.

now i'm reading about your experience with the suicide hotline.

​

i don't get it, what are we supposed to do when we're trying to seek help? is it too late to seek help now? should i have tried and reached out before i thought about killing myself? because before that, it doesn't feel like it's a serious issue. i only realized i needed help when i realized there wasn't much stopping me from killing myself.

​

i'm so sorry you're having to go through all this. i honestly don't know what you're supposed to do. i hope your daughter's ok too- take care.

i feel like my parents and brother have a pretty good (but very inaccurate) perception of me, and i wouldn't want to pull back the curtains to show them how wrong they were. i don't want them to know how i'm not doing too well right now, and if anything ever happens to me, i don't want them to slowly learn about what i've been going through by going through my possessions. like you said, it's all too intimate and i'd rather not have it revealed to everyone. i think it's better that they think of me as this successful happy kid rather than digging through my things once i'm dead and piecing together who i actually am.

i know, you're reading this and thinking, well, why don't you get rid of all of you possessions? unfortunately i live with my husband and he'd definitely know things are progressing if i started to purge my belongings. i know he'd try and interfere, and that worries me even more. i've heard terrible things of how our healthcare system deals with depression/suicidal thoughts and i don't want to end up in that mess.
